previous_scene.title: The Beginning of a Kansas Storm (Turn 1)
previous_scene.text:
The air tightens with a sudden charge, smelling of rain and dust. I’m standing at the doorway of the farmhouse, Toto tucked against my side as the wind shifts, the front yard flattening into a pale, pressing gray. Uncle Henry shoots to his feet with a rough urgency, his broad shoulders braced as he calls Em to attention. "There’s a cyclone coming, Em," he says, and I glimpse the worry tightening his jaw before he pivots toward the sheds, already moving as if the ground beneath us might tilt and slide.

Em’s hands leave the chores in a spray of suds and movement; the kitchen light flickers as she steps to the door with that practical, stubborn grace she keeps about her. Her voice sharp, she orders me, her eyes meeting mine with the weight of a plan formed in an instant. "Quick, Dorothy! Run for the cellar!" She doesn’t ask; she tells, and in that moment, Toto and I become part of a doorway I’m certain I’ll never forget.

Toto wiggles in my arms, sensing the shift in the air, and with a tiny, urgent sound he slips from my grasp. He twists, smaller than a shadow, and darts toward the shelter of the bed where he’s learned to hide in storms. I watch him vanish under the bed with a tremor in the room—an animal’s instinct, a small flare of fear—and the reality of fear settles over me like the first cold touch of rain.

The house hums with the building tension of wind and weather. Outside, the wind’s voice grows louder, a cruel drumbeat against the walls, while inside, the family moves with practiced certainty. I grip Toto’s leash (though he’s already vanished from my reach) and take a step toward the cellar, my feet careful on the creaky floorboards, my heart pounding with a stubborn courage I’m not sure I own yet. The storm is coming. I know it.

cases.name: captured-missing-fall
cases.text: Dust and wind crowd the doorway as I gather Toto back into my arms, parting the tangle of memory to focus on the doorway between safety and the storm. I slip my fingers beneath Toto, easing him from under the bed where he hid, his little whines soft with fear and trust. The air tastes of rain and grit as Aunt Em’s voice cuts through the growing roar outside, sharp with command, and the trapdoor thuds open with a wooden groan I feel in my bones. She slides down the ladder into the cellar, her presence vanishing into the black earth below, leaving me with the dog in my arms and the ceiling’s tremor answering the cyclone’s breath. I move, careful as a cat across the floorboards, Toto tucked against my chest, eyes bright and ears listening to the world gone loud with wind. The room tilts and the house shudders, but I am fixed on the doorway, on the thin thread of path that leads to Aunt Em’s safety and Toto’s warmth. I reach the edge of the trap and, with a breath that tastes of Kansas dust and resolve, draw Toto closer and begin the slow, uncertain walk toward the cellar’s mouth.

cases.name: correct-seated-ending
cases.text: I bend beside the bed and reach for Toto, who is still underneath it. Aunt Em throws open the trapdoor and climbs down the ladder while I am still reaching. I catch Toto and hold him against my chest. With Aunt Em now below in the cellar, I start across the room toward the open trapdoor. Halfway across, the house shakes and I lose my footing, sitting down hard on the floor. I remain seated there holding Toto; we have not reached the cellar.
